parsed.explanation: The dossier documents state-directed enforcement against gender-nonconforming people: a dedicated trans-specific detention power (six months without charge for 'impersonating'), arrests in public solely on gender expression, documented custodial beatings and sexual harassment (2019–2022), dating-app entrapment of a foreign visitor (44 days, no lawyer, no translator), and an airline employee detained, struck, and deported over appearance. Criminalisation of same-sex conduct, illegal cohabitation, and torture/conversion-therapy accounts compound severity. This is tier-1/2 organised state targeting with no working remedy. It sits just above the 0.05 tier because no execution pathway is credibly applied to trans visitors, but far below any 0.25 anchor: enforcement is recent, systematic, and visitor-facing.

entry_documents.exposure: Cohabitation illegal; hotels documented refusing same-sex couples or requiring concealment; appearance-based arrests of visitors documented (airline employee, tourists). No documented marker-check regime, but gender-expression-based street and venue enforcement reaches visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Organiser pledged to remind hotels of non-discrimination requirements; head of state said visitors welcome. None shown to operate against actual enforcement.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch or appearance at check-in can trigger police referral into the detention regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Six months' detention without trial for 'impersonating the opposite gender'; beatings, torture, sexual harassment in custody; forced detransition and conversion therapy reported (authorities deny); dating-app entrapment with 44-day detention; medication denial.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention flows from gender expression alone; foreign nationalities reported targeted post-tournament.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custody placement conditions not detailed; forced medical procedures on trans detainees reported.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Trans detainees moved toward conversion 'therapy' on release (resident-facing but part of regime character).

care_services.exposure: Denial of antiretroviral medication to detainees documented; forced detransition reported.
care_services.interaction: Care access collapses once trans/LGB status is discovered in custody.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State frames gender expression as 'impersonation', 'public morality' and 'prostitution' offences; police told detainee he had no rights; rainbow flags subject to confiscation; advocacy criminalised; protesters arrested.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police are primary perpetrators; complaints offer no realistic recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific rules documented; the general enforcement regime (appearance-based arrest, six-month detention) would apply regardless of age; travelling with a partner adds cohabitation exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's outing through any police stop could cascade to the minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police conduct public arrests solely on gender expression; unlawful searches; officers themselves commit beatings and sexual harassment.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; police response is the harm.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police engagement with any gender-nonconforming visitor creates direct violence risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No effective remedy documented: detainee denied lawyer and translator; UN working group raised concerns; informer coercion reported; state denies abuses.
remedies_unknowns.protection: UN attention documented but produced no shown relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Theoretical capital sentence for Muslims via religious courts unresolved but unimposed; regional entry-ban proposal shelved, status unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Shares street sweeps, custodial violence, torture and forced medical procedures. Differs: no documented death from custody and no execution pathway credibly applied to trans visitors; capital sentence is theoretical and never imposed. Sits just above 0.05.

Very similar: entrapment, arrests based on gender expression, beatings in custody, conversion practices, no effective recourse, imprisonment plausible. The documented six-month trans-specific detention power and visitor cases place it squarely at this tier.
0.25-D involves blackmail and selective enforcement with some appellate relief. This dossier shows torture, no functioning remedy, and state-run detention of trans people, materially worse than 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of state-directed targeting of gender-nonconforming people: a dedicated no-charge detention power, criminalised conduct, criminalised cohabitation, entrapment, and documented custodial torture and sexual harassment reaching visitors, with no working remedy and police as perpetrators. Visitor-facing enforcement is recent and systematic (2016–2023), not residual. The contested forced-detransion account and theoretical capital sentence add uncertainty but the verified record alone sits in the severe band. Protections are rhetorical only (tournament welcome statements) and are contradicted by simultaneous enforcement. Rating near 0.13, just above the lethal-outcome tier.
